topic: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations (PDEs): Modeling a Changing World

sections.title: The Hook: Leo the Lizard and the Hot Rock
lecture_lines: Meet Leo, sunbathing on a warm, desert rock.
The rock's temperature varies by position and time.
Ordinary equations track change over just one variable.
But PDEs track change across space and time simultaneously.
They model how heat flows through the entire rock.
animations: Create a simple lizard shape on a grey rectangle.
Color the rock with a gradient #FF4500 to #FFD700.
Show a simple line graph moving forward in time.
Expand the graph into a 2D grid pulsing with color.
Show heat ripples #FF0000 moving outward from a center point.

sections.title: Prerequisite Bridge: From Derivatives to Partials
lecture_lines: Imagine hiking across a steep, 3D mountain range.
A partial derivative finds the slope in one direction.
We hold all other variables constant while measuring change.
animations: Draw a 2D curve with a tangent line #00FF00.
Show a grid where only one axis is highlighted #00BFFF.
Display "∂f/∂x" and "∂f/∂y" with arrows pointing along axes.

sections.title: Defining the PDE: The Multi-Variable Balance
lecture_lines: A PDE relates a function's partial derivatives together.
Consider the heat equation: change over time equals curvature.
The solution isn't one number, but a whole field.
This field represents values across every point in space.
We use special symbols to denote these partial changes.
animations: Display "u(x, t)" in the center of the screen.
Highlight "∂" in the Heat Equation #FFFF00.
Transform "u" into a surface of shifting colors.
Write "∂u/∂t = α(∂²u/∂x²)" and underline the derivatives.
Flash the spatial derivative "∂²u/∂x²" with a glow #FF8C00.

sections.title: Visualizing the Dynamics: The Vibrating String
lecture_lines: A plucked guitar string demonstrates the wave equation.
Its curvature determines the force pulling it back.
This force creates acceleration, changing its velocity over time.
PDEs link the string's shape to its future motion.
Watch how the wave travels through the material.
animations: Draw a horizontal line #FFFFFF representing a string.
Deform the string into a sine wave shape.
Show arrows #FF0000 pulling the curve toward the center.
Animate the sine wave oscillating up and down.
Pulse the entire string with a light blue glow #ADD8E6.

sections.title: Application: Designing a Cooling System
lecture_lines: Engineers use PDEs to optimize cooling for electronics.
We simulate heat flowing away from a hot CPU.
This prevents overheating before a physical prototype exists.
animations: Show a square "CPU" #FF4500 with heat lines.
Animate red flow #FF0000 moving into blue pipes #0000FF.
Transition the CPU color from red to cool blue.

sections.title: Summary: The Language of the Universe
lecture_lines: PDEs describe everything from weather to quantum mechanics.
They balance rates of change across our complex world.
Master PDEs to decode the fundamental laws of nature.
animations: Cycle through symbols: water drop, speaker, flame, spark.
Display "Balancing Rates" with rotating gears #C0C0C0.
Zoom out to show a dark blue starfield #191970.
